memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And now the cry of the Israelites has reached me, and I have seen the way the Egyptians are oppressing them. So now, go. I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring my people the Israelites out of Egypt." - Exodus 3:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God has just described a magnificent rescue that He Himself will accomplish. Then comes the turn: so now, go. I am sending you.

The God who could have delivered Israel with a word chooses instead to send a man. He almost always does. He fed the five thousand through a boy's lunch. He reached the nations through ordinary apostles. He usually answers prayers about human need by sending a human being.

That should unsettle us a little. When we pray about a lonely neighbour, a struggling family member, an injustice in our workplace — we should be ready for God to answer with go.

Notice also that God's compassion and God's commission come in the same breath. He is moved by suffering, and He moves people toward it. Care that never becomes action was never really care.

Jesus said it plainly: as the Father sent Me, I am sending you (Jn 20:21). Every believer is a sent person.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a need I have prayed about that God may be asking me to address?
2. Where has my compassion stopped short of actually going?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I pray about a need, make me willing to be part of the answer. Send me, and give me courage to go. Amen.
